question: Since October 2023, 238 fishermen have been murdered by Israel in Gaza, including after the ceasefire agreement1.

While around 110 000 Gazans depended on the fishing sector before the genocide began, the industry is now at risk: vessels and fishing infrastructure have been destroyed by Israel, materials needed to repair vessels have been subject to a blockade, access to the sea is strictly limited and fishermen are systematically targeted by Israeli gunfire2.

Catches of fish – a vital source of protein for Gazans – have fallen to an all-time low. The 15 tonnes that could once be caught in a single day now take more than a month to reel in3. The destruction of the fisheries sector is starving the Palestinian people, driving their economy to collapse and completely eroding their resilience. With this in mind: 1.

What action does the Commission intend to take to support the Gazan fisheries sector, including by providing financial support for the acquisition of the necessary equipment and ensuring safe access to the sea, in order to continually ensure the Gazan people’s right to food?
What action does the Commission intend to take to stop the Israeli blockade, which, in particular, deprives Palestinians of the materials needed to repair and maintain fishing vessels?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.11.2026) The Commission is committed to contributing to the implementation of the UN comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict in line with UN Security Council Resolution (UNSCR) 28031. The Commission adopted the ‘Commission Implementing Decision on the implementation of the special measure II in favour of Palestine2 for 2026-2027’3 in July 2026.

The Action Document for Early recovery support to Gaza4 with a total amount of EUR 80 million aims at enhancing and rehabilitating basic social and economic infrastructure meeting the needs of local communities. This action was informed by the Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment5, whereas the fisheries sector falls under short-term priority actions under the productive sector.

It may include activities such as providing basic support to the private sector to preserve/resume businesses. Furthermore, the Commission launched the Team Gaza Initiative at the second meeting of the Palestine Donor Group in July 2026 under the shared commitment to advance the UNSCR 2803.

It brings together 17 Member States and international actors and an amount of close to EUR 900 million for early recovery projects in Gaza, strengthening donor coordination and supporting joint advocacy efforts.

The EU is coordinating closely with all actors on the ground in Gaza, including with the Palestinian Authority, UN partners, the US, Israeli authorities, as well as the Board of Peace, to facilitate access of goods and services and to ensure enabling conditions are met for the implementation of the projects.
1 https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/4093207?v=pdf. 2 The designation of Palestine shall not be construed as recognition of a State of Palestine and is without
